cohort: The study included 89 patients who underwent diagnostic conization due to HPV persistence, repeated cytological abnormalities, type 3 transformation zone, and the inability to retrieve a relevant cervical histology sample.
finding: Diagnostic conization in patients with cervical stenosis, high-risk HPV persistence, and repeated cytological abnormalities revealed a high prevalence of undetected high-grade cervical dysplasia and early-stage cervical carcinoma (53.9% histological abnormalities, 25.8% CIN 2+, 2.3% early-stage cervical carcinoma).
